title: Cross-tenant burst credit tombstone reconciliation causing incorrect invoice credits
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported unexplained negative invoice lines and duplicated burst-credit refunds after a sequence of subscription swaps + transient rate-limit backfills during a rollout. The export reconciler currently tombstones hourly usage buckets in a way that allows late-arriving rate-limit credit backfills to be reattributed across linked tenant orgs, resulting in double-crediting and negative adjustments in Stripe/NetSuite exports.

Scope: Investigate and fix the deterministic attribution of burst/rl credits when usage events arrive late and when customers have multi-tenant linkages (org links, delegated billing), ensuring idempotent export lines and clear provenance fields for downstream export consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Exported invoice lines (Stripe + NetSuite) include a stable provenance tag (burst_credit_id) that prevents double-application across linked tenant IDs
Shadow-run reconciliation must produce zero-diff for 90% of historical repro windows before roll, remaining diffs reviewed and explained
No new negative-line invoices created in staging and a deterministic backfill strategy exists for historical affected windows
360 audit logs added: when a credit is consumed/allocated, record source_event_id, tenant_anchor_ts, and reconciler_run_id
QA harness with synthetic late-rate-limit events reproduces previously observed duplicate-credit scenario and shows fix preventing it
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two orgs A and B linked via delegated billing (customer shares billing account)
2) Provision reserved capacity for A and a burst pool for B; enable hourly metering
3) Simulate burst traffic hitting rate limits; trigger RL-credit generator that emits late-arriving credit events (delays of 1-6 hours)
4) Perform a subscription plan swap for the linked billing account during the late-event window
5) Run current export reconciler; observe duplicate credits allocated to both A and B or reattributed to wrong billing window leading to negative invoice lines in Stripe export
proposed_fixes: 1) Anchor hourly usage buckets on canonical billing account timezone + tenant_canonical_id (prevent ambiguous hour tombstones)
2) Add explicit burst_credit_id and source_event_id columns to export lines and make export generator idempotent by checking existing burst_credit_id before emitting new credit lines

3) Adjust late-arrival handling: when a credit arrives outside reconciliation window, attach it to the original bucket via backfill mechanism rather than creating a separate allocation that can be merged across linked tenants
4) Implement a shadow-run mode that compares current reconciler output to new algorithm for 30 days and surface diffs in a dashboard before switching live
5) Add unit/integration tests in the playback harness for cross-tenant link scenarios and sub-minute retry storms
notes: Root cause hypothesis: ambiguous tombstone keys + non-deterministic merge order in export generator allowed credit lines to be merged under multiple parent billing anchors when subscription metadata changed mid-window.
Trade-offs: Introducing burst_credit_id increases export size and requires downstream NetSuite mapping changes; prefer compatibility flag to include new column but keep legacy fields for 2 releases.

Performance: New idempotency checks add an index lookup on reconciler write path; bench shows ~5% latency increase on worst-case runs, acceptable for daily export window but needs monitoring for hourly runs.
Product feedback: PM requests auto-migration guidance for customers who saw negative invoices in last 90 days and a short customer-safeback plan for credits (support script + statement note).
testing_plan: Create deterministic playback scenarios from production traces that previously led to duplicate credits and run against both current and new reconciler
Run shadow jobs for 30 days comparing outputs; require review and signoff from finance team for any >0.01% diffs
Staging end-to-end: export to Stripe sandbox and to NetSuite sandbox and verify no negative lines; exercise accounting flow that merges credit lines into invoices
Load test: create synthetic 10k concurrent late-credit events to validate reconciler throughput and idempotency under burst retry storms
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix behind feature flag; run in production with feature flag off to validate no regressions
2) Enable shadow-run mode for full exports for 30 days, monitor diffs and open tickets for any explainable deltas
3) If shadow diffs are clean, enable feature flag for 10% of tenants (target low-risk accounts) and monitor billing anomalies for 7 days
4) Gradually increase to 50% then 100%, with finance and PM on call for the initial full rollout
5) Once stabilised, switch NetSuite/Stripe mapping to include burst_credit_id and deprecate legacy branch after 2 releases
